target_customer: Restaurants and restaurant software vendors in Latin America that need orders and payments connected to delivery apps and POS systems
problem: Restaurants in Latin America juggle several delivery apps, POS systems and payment tools that do not talk to each other.
business_model: API and software subscription connecting restaurant tech services

founders.name: Orlando Espinoza
previous_startups: Karta (credit card service for foreigners in the US, outcome not researched)

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many fragmented POS and delivery platform APIs across countries is routine but laborious engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations are copyable, though each connected restaurant creates some switching cost.

market_need_then: Restaurants in Latin America were adopting delivery apps such as Uber Eats and Rappi in 2019, creating a need for order consolidation; no quantitative evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with several unrelated MiPOS companies in Malaysia, Australia and Ecuador, and no brand evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: Mipos.dev joined YC in Summer 2019 to connect Latin American restaurant tech and is listed as Inactive. The cause of the shutdown is not public: no post-mortem or news was found, so no failure factors are asserted. A separate Ecuador based MiPOS from the same founders received Magma Partners investment in 2019, which may be the same business under another name.
notes: mipos.dev could not be fetched because the host did not resolve in this session's network, so the site may not be dead; the YC status is Inactive. Magma Partners (published 2019-09-10) says MiPOS, founded by the same two names in 2019 in Quito, went through YC and received an undisclosed investment; whether it is the same entity is unconfirmed. Latka funding figures are contradictory and a loot-drop summary of failure reasons is AI-assisted, so both were not used. Competitor searches returned only 2025 to 2026 material, so none are listed as of founding.
